name: Joab
bio:
Joab was the son of Zeruiah, brother of Abishai and Asahel, and David's most important military commander — fierce, ruthless, and loyal to David's dynasty, yet repeatedly acting on his own authority and without scruple.

When Abner installed Ish-Bosheth as king and war broke out with the house of David, Joab's forces clashed with Abner's at the pool of Gibeon, beginning with a contest between young men and escalating into full battle, which Joab's side won. Joab's brother Asahel, swift as a wild gazelle, chased Abner relentlessly; Abner warned him off several times, reluctant to kill him, but Asahel would not turn aside, so Abner struck him dead with the butt of his spear (2 Samuel 2:12-23).

When Abner later defected to David and came to Hebron to negotiate peace, David welcomed him and sent him away safely; but Joab, on learning of it, angrily confronted David for letting Abner go, then secretly sent messengers to bring him back, pulled him aside at the city gate under pretense of private conversation, and stabbed him to death in revenge for Asahel (2 Samuel 3:22-27). David was furious and publicly cursed Joab's house, yet could do nothing against Zeruiah's two sons, saying, "Today... I am weak, though anointed king, and these men, the sons of Zeruiah, are too strong for me" (2 Samuel 3:28-39). Joab's continued, often overreaching role throughout David's unification of Israel and the founding of his dynasty unfolds in detail through the rest of 2 Samuel.
